cpu_share.provenance: chosen by the owner 2026-11-16: the test runners may use 90 percent of the logical processors at once, because one sequential suite left the machine at 20 to 25 percent CPU; a number above 0 and at most 1, overridden by -Jobs

poll_ms.provenance: chosen 2026-11-16, unmeasured: milliseconds between two looks at the running child processes, short against a suite that lasts seconds

split_seconds.provenance: chosen 2026-11-16 after one run: a single suite (the privacy guard, 122 tests that start git, a shell and a scanner) took 12 minutes alone while the rest ended in about 2, leaving the machine at 10 percent CPU; a suite whose recorded time is at least this many seconds is split by test into several processes

chunk_seconds.provenance: chosen 2026-11-16, unmeasured: the work a split suite is cut into, in seconds of recorded time per process, so a 720-second suite becomes 12 processes, never more than the number of jobs or of tests
